state_limits: Child HEAD equals parent pin; git status --short --untracked-files=all was empty. No model services, databases, credentials, containers or tests were run.
description: A FastAPI proxy intended to add session history, safety checks, RAG, embeddings/reranking, tool calls, quotas and scheduling in front of OpenAI-compatible model servers.
scope_audience: Developers operating local LLM services who want a configurable proxy; README makes broad compatibility and safety claims that were not verified in this read-only assessment.

creativity.reason: Combining server-side session, retrieval, quota and tool controls in a transparent proxy is a useful integration thesis; novelty is unknown.

current_usefulness.reason: Source exposes chat, embedding, rerank and passthrough endpoints, but no running service or feature-complete behavior was verified.

expected_usefulness.reason: If the stated proxy capabilities were complete and dependable, they could be important for local LLM operators; security and compatibility are central unverified conditions.

impl_progress.reason: A real FastAPI route layer and typed request/core logic exist, but the README spans many capabilities without evidence here for their complete behavior or acceptance.

presentability.reason: README has an extensive quickstart and feature descriptions, but deployment depends on several unpinned external services and the claims were not smoke-tested.

verification: README, app.py and core request/model definitions inspected; no tests, security review, endpoint compatibility test, database setup or model call.

evidence.locator: Core Features; Quick Start; Production Deployment

contribution: An implemented proxy/API scaffold exists, but the many README feature claims are not treated as established capabilities absent contract-focused source or runtime evidence.
alternatives_question: Which current local-LLM proxies provide the same session, retrieval, safety and tool-control behavior, and what contract-tested scenario would establish a distinct advantage?

delivery_likelihood.reason: There is substantial service code, but end-to-end behavior, deployment safety, compatibility and feature coverage were not verified.

reason: The implementation warrants retention as a serious attempt, but broad intended value and reliability cannot be inferred from feature claims or endpoint scaffolding.
next_step: Before promotion, inspect owned tests and verify one documented chat/session path plus a negative safety/tool-control case on an isolated local setup.
inspection_limits: No source projects were changed, installed, built, executed, tested, or accessed over a network; no child commits or pushes were made.
